papers.title_in_file: Tree tensor network state approach for solving hierarchical equations of motion
papers.version_note: arXiv:2304.05151v2 (3 Jun 2023). The text holds the main paper and the reference list only; the supplementary material (Frenkel exciton model, spin-boson-like chain, Pade expressions) is not in the text.
papers.what_it_is: A method paper that represents the extended wave function of the hierarchical equations of motion as a tree tensor network state, propagates it with a time-dependent variational principle algorithm, and benchmarks it on a spin-boson model against conventional HEOM and a matrix product state chain.

assertions.value: The authors describe the HEOM method as based on an exponential series expansion of the bath correlation function, used to construct a group of auxiliary density operators (ADOs) that obey a hierarchical set of differential equations.
quotes: The core idea of the method is based on an exponential series expansion of the bath correlation function
so as to construct a group of auxiliary density operators (ADOs) that obey a hierarchical set of differential equations.
assertions.certainty_reason: A description of an existing method that the paper attributes to earlier work.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper concerns classical tensor network simulation of open quantum system dynamics; it bears on the qc context only as a simulation method.

assertions.value: The authors state that HEOM applications are limited when the central system is large, many exponential terms (effective bath modes) are required, and a deep hierarchical depth is needed, because the computational cost grows exponentially with these factors.
quotes: its applications hit a hard wall in the cases where the central system size is large, many exponential terms (or effective bath modes) are required to reproduce the original bath correlation function
This is because the computational cost grows exponentially with the increase of these factors.
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement in the introduction without a derivation or measurement in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that, when entanglement stays confined within near neighboring tensors over a long time, the computational cost of the HEOM+MPS/TT method scales linearly with the system size, the number of effective bath modes, and the hierarchical depth.
quotes: confined within the near neighboring tensors over a long time, the computational cost of the HEOM+MPS/TT method scales linearly with the system size, the number of effective bath modes, and the hierarchical depth.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement about earlier HEOM+MPS/TT work, not shown in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that the HEOM+MPS/TT method often does not meet that condition, because the system degrees of freedom may be strongly coupled to every effective bath mode, so correlation spreads quickly along the MPS chain and very large bond dimensions are needed for accurate results.
quotes: the system DoF may also be strongly coupled to every effective bath mode. As a consequence, the correlation would quickly spread over a long distance along the MPS chain, and very large bond dimensions are needed to obtain accurate results.
assertions.certainty_reason: The motivating limitation is asserted, not measured in this paper; the later MPS test used the same bond dimension as the tree.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors' own MPS/TT test later in the paper converged at the same maximal bond dimension as the tree, so the motivating claim of very large bond dimensions is not exhibited by the one model they ran.

assertions.value: The authors take the spin-boson model as the demonstration system, with the spin coupled to a bath of harmonic oscillators through a linear form in the bath coordinates.
quotes: a simple but paradigmatic open quantum system, the spinboson model
takes a linear form with respect to the bath coordinate qj
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own model in Section 1 (Eqs. 1 to 5).

assertions.value: The authors adopt the Pade pole decomposition scheme for the exponential expansion of the bath correlation function and state that the infinite sum can be cut off at a finite P at finite temperatures, chosen large enough to reproduce the original correlation function well.
quotes: work, we adopt the Pad´e pole decomposition scheme19,49
At finite temperatures, the infinite summation in Eq. (9) can be cut off at a finite P , which is chosen large enough to well reproduce the original bath correlation function.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the decomposition it uses; the explicit expressions are in the supplementary material, which is not in the text.

assertions.value: The authors define the ADO label as an ordered set of P + 1 non-negative integers, each associated with a frequency component of the exponential expansion.
quotes: is an ordered set of P + 1 non-negative integers and each np is associated with a frequency component
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the ADO label here.

assertions.value: The authors describe the simplest truncation scheme as setting an ADO to zero when the sum of its occupation numbers exceeds the truncation tier L.
quotes: The simplest truncation scheme is to set ρn(t) = 0 when ∑p np > L and L is the hierarchical truncation tier.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the truncation it uses for the conventional HEOM comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that the HEOM hierarchy can be reformulated as a Schrodinger-like equation by introducing an effective phonon bath and the density matrix purification scheme, with an extended wave function formed from all ADOs.
quotes: via the introduction of an effective phonon bath and the density matrix purification scheme.
All the ADOs combined comprise an extended wave function in the enlarged space
the basis in the occupation number representation of a virtual dissipative
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the mapping and the extended wave function it propagates.

assertions.value: The authors state that with all effective bath modes in their ground states, the reduced system density operator is reproduced.
quotes: the reduced system density operator is reproduced, ρS(t) = ρ(0,⋯,0)(t).
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement of the construction the paper uses to read out system observables.

assertions.value: The authors state that the super Hamiltonian is non-Hermitian, so the norm of the extended wave function is not conserved.
quotes: the super Hamiltonian H is non-Hermitian. As such, the norm of the extended wave function
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this property of its own super Hamiltonian; no proof is given in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that direct time integration of the extended wave function equation is usually intractable, because the size of the coefficient tensor scales exponentially with the number of extended system degrees of freedom, N = Ns + P + 1.
quotes: is usually an intractable task as the size of the coefficient tensor Csn(t) scales exponentially with the number of extended system DoFs, N = Ns + P + 1.
assertions.certainty_reason: A scaling statement without a derivation in the text.

assertions.value: The authors define the bond dimension as a controllable parameter that can be systematically increased to reduce the degree of approximation of the MPS/TT form; the maximum over all bonds is the maximal bond dimension Dmax.
quotes: where the bond dimension Di is a controllable parameter, that can be systematically increased to reduce the
The maximum value
among {Di} is designated as the maximal bond dimension Dmax.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines Dmax, the parameter reported in the benchmark.

assertions.value: The authors describe the TTNS as an extension of MPS/TT beyond one dimension that accommodates a more complicated entanglement network; a general TTNS connects all tensors into a loop-free tree, so a unique path exists between any two tensors.
quotes: The TTNS is an extension of the MPS/TT beyond 1D geometry and thus can accommodate a more complicated entanglement network.
A general TTNS connects all tensors into a tree structure and the network is loop-free
exists a unique path between any two tensors.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the TTNS ansatz it uses.

assertions.value: The authors state that the TTNS is also called the hierarchical Tucker format, which is the ansatz behind multi configuration time-dependent Hartree and its multi-layer variant.
quotes: It is also called hierarchical Tucker format
quantum dynamics approach, multi configuration time-dependent Hartree and its multi-layer variant.
assertions.certainty_reason: A relation attributed to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that the tree in which every bath node attaches directly to the system node matches the entanglement topology of the super Hamiltonian, but its tensor network contraction cost can be very expensive or even intractable when many effective environmental modes are taken into account.
assertions.anchor: Tensor network states, p.4, Fig. 1 (b); the text layer prints the cost expression garbled
quotes: However, the tensor network contraction cost for this tree structure scales as
which can be very expensive or even intractable when many effective environmental modes are taken into account.
assertions.certainty_reason: A cost statement without a derivation in the text; the printed exponent is garbled.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints the cost as O(DmP +ax1); read as D_max to the power P + 1, the cost is exponential in the number of bath modes.

assertions.value: The authors state that inserting connecting nodes between the system node and the bath nodes resolves the cost issue, that a balanced tree suits equal effect of all modes and an unbalanced tree suits unequal effect, and that they use the unbalanced tree in Fig. 1 (d) because they expect higher Pade pole numbers to matter less.
quotes: This issue can be resolved by inserting connecting nodes (yellow-shaded) between the system node and bath nodes
Otherwise, a more unbalanced tree structure can be adopted when the influence of some effective virtual phonon modes on the system dynamics is much stronger than the others.
It is likely, that the impact of the effective phonon modes with a large Pad
we adopt the unbalanced TTNS in Fig. 1 (d) in our simulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: The tree choice is a design decision; its rationale is an author expectation (likely), not tested against the balanced tree.
assertions.reader_inference: The balanced tree and the star tree are not benchmarked in the text, so the choice of the unbalanced tree is untested against them.

assertions.value: The authors state that Yan and Shi proposed an efficient split operator method for propagating the binary TTNS, and that this work instead applies the TDVP time propagation scheme directly on the whole TTNS.
quotes: Yan and Shi71 proposed an efficient split operator method for propagating the binary TTNS.
In this work, we present an alternative route that directly employs the TDVP time propagation scheme on the whole TTNS.
assertions.certainty_reason: The prior method is attributed to cited work; the paper does not compare against it.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no comparison with the Yan and Shi method.

assertions.value: The authors state that the one-site TDVP algorithm projects the wave function into the tangent space, a manifold of all TTNSs with fixed bond dimensions, and integrates the projected equation locally, updating each node tensor and each link tensor in a specified sequence; they cite earlier work for the derivation and state that TDVP has been proven stable and efficient for MPS/TT.
quotes: i.e., a manifold of all TTNSs with fixed bond dimensions
can be integrated locally, where each tensor T [k] and the link V [km] between node k and one of its neighboring node m in a specified sequence are updated according to the following equations
TDVP algorithm has been proven to be a stable and efficient time propagation scheme for the MPS/TT.
assertions.certainty_reason: The algorithm and its stability are attributed to cited work; the paper gives no proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that a full TDVP step starts from a canonicalized TTNS with all tensors except the root orthonormalized, and a full sweep starts and ends at the root node; for the example tree the path is 1 → 2 → 1 → 3 → 4 → 3 → 5 → 6 → 5 → 7 → 5 → 3 → 1.
quotes: A full TDVP step starts from a canonicalized TTNS, where all tensors except for the root node are orthonormalized
A full sweeping procedure starts and ends at the root node
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the sweep it implements.

assertions.value: The authors report a spin-boson benchmark with the spin initially in the spin-up state and parameters ϵ = 50 cm−1, ∆ = 200 cm−1, β−1 = 300K, λ = 100 cm−1, and Ω = 10 cm−1.
quotes: The spin is initially placed
in the spin-up state. The parameters can be found in the
The following parameters are used: ϵ = 50 cm−1, ∆ = 200 cm−1, β−1 = 300K, λ = 100 cm−1, and Ω = 10 cm−1.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own benchmark parameters in the Fig. 3 caption.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use a much smaller value for Ω than for the other parameters, which indicates slow bath relaxation compared with the other system dynamical processes.
quotes: value for Ω than other parameters, which indicates that
the bath relaxation is slow as compared to other system
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the regime of its benchmark, which limits what the benchmark shows.
assertions.reader_inference: The benchmark is one parameter set in a slow bath regime and one model, so it does not show behavior at other regimes.

assertions.value: The authors report that the conventional HEOM result converged at a hierarchical truncation tier L = 50 with P = 3, and that the HEOM+TTNS method took 0 ≤ np ≤ L for every effective bath mode, which means more ADOs are taken into account than in the conventional method.
quotes: Dynamics of the spin-boson model calculated using the conventional HEOM with a hierarchical truncation tier L = 50 and the HEOM+TTNS method with a maximal bond dimension Dmax = 5.
and P = 3. Using the HEOM+TTNS method with the TTNS
For every effective bath mode, we take 0 ≤ np ≤ L, which means that actually more ADOs are taken into account than in the conventional HEOM method.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the settings of its own runs.

assertions.value: The authors report that with a maximal bond dimension Dmax = 5 the HEOM+TTNS result for the spin dynamics is in excellent agreement with the conventional HEOM result, as shown in Fig. 3 (b).
quotes: We found that with a very low maximal bond dimension Dmax = 5, the result obtained through the HEOM+TTNS method is already in excellent agreement with that obtained through the conventional HEOM method, as shown in Fig. 3 (b).
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on one model and one parameter set, judged from a plotted curve; no error value is given.
assertions.reader_inference: The agreement is shown only graphically; the text gives no error measure.

assertions.value: The authors report that all codes are written in the Julia programming language and the simulations run on a single CPU core of an Apple MacBook Pro laptop with an M1 chip.
quotes: all the codes are written using Julia programming language and our simulations are run on a single CPU core of an Apple MacBook Pro laptop with M1 chip.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the platform of its own timings.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for the conventional HEOM method with an exponential integrator, every simulation step takes on average 6.7 seconds with a time step ∆t = 0.025 fs and requires a memory of 7.6 GB.
quotes: we use an exponential integrator as proposed in Ref. 79, which requires less memory usage as compared to RungeKutta methods.
Every simulation step takes on average 6.7 seconds with a time step ∆t = 0.025 fs and requires a memory of 7.6 GB.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical timing from one study on one machine.

assertions.value: The authors report that with the HEOM+TTNS method every simulation step takes only 0.028 seconds in CPU time with memory usage of 10 MB, and that the maximally allowed time step is ∆t = 0.5 fs, much larger than for the conventional method.
quotes: Every simulation step takes only 0.028 seconds in CPU time and memory usage of 10 MB.
it is also found that the maximally allowed time step in the HEOM+TTNS method is ∆t = 0.5 fs, much larger than that used in the conventional HEOM method.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical timing from one study on one machine and one model.
assertions.reader_inference: The per step ratio is about 240 (6.7 s over 0.028 s), but the text does not say which time step the 0.028 s figure used, and the two methods use different time steps, so the ratio for a fixed propagation time is not given.

assertions.value: The authors state that their conventional HEOM code is not fully optimized and that the filtering algorithm of Shi et al. would greatly improve its efficiency.
quotes: our code for the conventional HEOM method is not fully optimized.
would greatly improve its efficiency.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit on its own speed comparison.
assertions.reader_inference: The reported speed gain is measured against a conventional implementation the authors call not fully optimized.

assertions.value: The authors state that the HEOM+TTNS simulation time grows nearly linearly with the pole number P and truncation tier L, in contrast to the factorial scaling of the conventional method, and that the method is generally much faster even for the relatively simple spin-boson model.
quotes: the simulation time using the HEOM+TTNS method grows nearly linearly with the increase of pole number P and truncation tier L, in contrast to the factorial scaling in the conventional HEOM method.
assertions.certainty_reason: A scaling statement with no scaling data shown in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: The benchmark uses one value of P and one value of L for each method, so the scaling is not exhibited in the text.

assertions.value: The authors report that the HEOM+MPS/TT method also converges with a maximal bond dimension Dmax = 5 (data not shown) but that every simulation step is four times slower than with the HEOM+TTNS method, using the same time propagation algorithm and code.
quotes: The same time propagation algorithm and code as in the HEOM+TTNS method are used.

For this model, although we found that the result of the HEOM+MPS/TT method (data not shown) also converges with a maximal bond dimension of Dmax = 5, every simulation step is four times slower than that of the HEOM+TTNS method.
This implies the pure influence of a tree shape in determining the practical computational cost.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on one model; the MPS/TT data are not shown.
assertions.reader_inference: The MPS/TT converges at the same Dmax as the tree, so the advantage reported here is a constant factor on this model, not the rank advantage the introduction motivates.

assertions.value: The authors state that the matrix product operator form of the super Hamiltonian for the MPS/TT test is obtained using the ITensor package.
quotes: the matrix product operator format of the super Hamiltonian H is obtained using ITensor Package.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states how its MPS/TT comparison was built.

assertions.value: The authors state that the demonstration is a proof of concept on the spin-boson model, that the method can be generalized to much more complicated systems, and that the supplementary material shows its applicability to the Frenkel exciton model and a spin-boson-like chain model; the supplementary material is not in the text read.
quotes: As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrated in the main text the algorithm and results specific to the spin-boson model.
The method can be generalized to much more complicated systems.
In the SI, we show the applicability of the HEOM+TTNS method for the Frenkel exciton model
assertions.certainty_reason: The generalization is asserted; the supporting results are in material not in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: The main text holds one model, one parameter set and one bond dimension; the generalization rests on the supplementary results.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they presented the feasibility of a genuine TTNS with a TDVP based time propagation algorithm for HEOM, compared with conventional HEOM and HEOM-MPS/TT, expect the method to benefit from advances developed for MPS/TT, and plan to extend it to open fermionic systems.
quotes: a genuine TTNS and TDVP-based time propagation algorithm for solving the HEOM method, and compared its performance to the conventional HEOM method as well as the HEOM-MPS/TT scheme.
we expect that the proposed HEOM+TTNS method can also benefit from algorithmic optimizations and advances that have been developed in the context of the MPS/TT representation.
we will extend the current approach to study open fermionic system problems in our future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: A conclusion and outlook; the expectation is an author claim.

assertions.value: The authors state in the abstract that the benchmark calculations on the spin-boson model with a slow-relaxing bath show consistent results with conventional HEOM while the computation is considerably sped up, and that the simulation with a genuine TTNS is four times faster than a one-dimensional matrix product state decomposition scheme.
quotes: Our benchmark calculations based on the spin-boson model with a slow-relaxing bath show that the proposed HEOM+TTNS approach yields consistent results with that of the conventional HEOM method, while the computation is considerably sped up.
the simulation with a genuine TTNS is four times faster than a one-dimensional matrix product state decomposition scheme.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on one model.
